title: Shared nonlinear encoder with low-rank latent Koopman regime Views
hypothesis: A shared invertible nonlinear coordinate map plus compact regime coordinates over stable latent linear dynamics recovers held-out regime compositions with lower complete bytes than independent Koopman operators while maintaining long-horizon stability and forecast quality.
insertion: latent transition only: A(a,b)=A0+a*B1+b*B2; shared encoder/decoder is fixed across regimes

latent_system.encoder: known orthogonal Q with x=tanh(Qz); inverse is arctanh(x)Q

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after native conditional low-rank alias or frozen gate miss.

controls: shared latent operator without regime code
Mirror regime coordinates over shared operators
native additive low-rank conditional latent dynamics
pass_gate: Heldout horizon-40 nRMSE <=0.02, max spectral radius <1, at least 25% fewer complete bytes than independent, and strict frontier gain over native low-rank conditional dynamics.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim on native low-rank alias, quality miss, unstable operator, storage gate miss, or no strict frontier gain.

compute.active_MACs: three dense maps per step for independent latent transition+forcing+decode; five maps for direct rank-2 conditional transition+forcing+decode
compute.wall_time: small CPU nonlinear-coordinate rollout calibration; not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic known nonlinear conjugacy and linear latent operators only; no trained Deep Koopman or nonlinear-system discovery claim.
Regime factor codes are known and charged; no regime inference claim.
The inverse encoder is deterministic from paid orthogonal Q and arctanh; no separate inverse matrix is stored.
Native conditional low-rank dynamics is the direct attribution control.
